mainTopic: Blemishes (מומין) of a בכור: testicles, legs, broken bones, אילא's list, eyes, mouth, tongue and jaw, after closing the discussion of the אצבע measure
overview: This amud opens in the middle of a quoted משנה about two measuring-cubits kept in שושן הבירה. Both were slightly longer than משה's cubit, so that Temple artisans would be paid by the smaller measure and work by the larger one, and never come to מעילה. רב נחמן בר יצחק then links the ברייתא's quarter-טפח אצבע to the tail blemish in our משנה instead. A new משנה discusses an animal with missing testicles. The גמרא rereads it to explain the argument between רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא, and explains the dispute between רבי עקיבא and רבי יוחנן בן נורי over a testicle found stuck to the loins: for רבי יוחנן בן נורי, eating it is eating קדשים בחוץ. Next come leg blemishes (extra or missing legs, closed hooves, שחול, כסול), where רב הונא and רב פפא set their limits. Then a hidden broken leg bone, and אילא's list of מומין in יבנה with his three additions. The גמרא resolves a contradiction about round human-like eyes and identifies the tongue rule as רבי יהודה's view. The amud ends with רבן גמליאל's case of a protruding lower jaw, which shows that the pig-mouth dispute covers only an overlapping upper lip.

steps.title: The two cubit-measures in שושן הבירה
steps.stepSummary: The quoted משנה describes two measuring cubits kept in שושן הבירה. One was longer than משה's cubit by half an אצבע, and the other was longer by a full אצבע.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the שושן הבירה chamber, one was at the northeast corner and one was at the southeast corner. The northeast one was longer than משה's cubit by half a fingerbreadth. The southeast one was longer than that one by another half a fingerbreadth. So it turns out to be longer than משה's cubit by a full fingerbreadth.
steps.whatsHappening: This amud begins in the middle of a quoted משנה. The גמרא is citing it as the first candidate for the 'fingerbreadth' the ברייתא was talking about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are three cubits in the picture. The first is משה's standard cubit. The second is one that is half an אצבע longer, and the third is one that is a full אצבע longer. Because these measures differ by fractions of a fingerbreadth, the exact size of an אצבע matters here.

keyTerms.meaning: A chamber over the eastern gate of the הר הבית, where the reference measures were kept
A fingerbreadth, which is one quarter of a טפח
משה's standard cubit, equal to six טפחים

steps.confusionAlert: This amud starts mid-sentence. The words 'one at the northeast corner' refer to two cubit-measures (אמות) that were named just before this amud begins.

phrases.english: in the Shushan HaBirah chamber,
phrases.notes: Continuation of the quote: 'There were two cubits...'

phrases.english: one on the northeast corner
and one on the southeast corner.
The one on the northeast corner

phrases.aramaic: הָיְתָה יְתֵירָה עַל שֶׁל מֹשֶׁה חֲצִי אֶצְבַּע,
phrases.english: was longer than Moshe's cubit by half a fingerbreadth,
and the one on the southeast corner
was longer than that one by another half fingerbreadth;

phrases.aramaic: נִמְצֵאת יְתֵירָה עַל שֶׁל מֹשֶׁה אֶצְבַּע.
phrases.english: so it turns out longer than Moshe's cubit by a full fingerbreadth.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּשׁוּשַׁן הַבִּירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the quotation that began on the previous amud, as the first identification of the ברייתא's אצבע.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two reference cubits existed, larger than משה's cubit by ½ אצבע and by 1 אצבע respectively.

steps.title: Why there was a large and a small measure
steps.stepSummary: The משנה explains the purpose of the different sizes. Artisans were paid by the small measure and worked by the large measure, so they would never overcharge the הקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why was one large and one small? So that the craftsmen would take payment by the small one and give back work by the large one, so that they would not come to misuse Temple property.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה asks and answers its own question: what is the point of having measures of different sizes?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a worker is paid for even a tiny bit more than he actually built, he has benefited from Temple property, which is מעילה. Measuring his pay by the smaller cubit and his work by the larger one builds in a safety margin, so the Temple always comes out slightly ahead.

keyTerms.meaning: Misusing or benefiting from הקדש (consecrated property)

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a classic principle of the Sages: they deliberately build in a margin of safety so that people never even come close to an איסור.

phrases.aramaic: וְלָמָה הָיוּ אַחַת גְּדוֹלָה וְאַחַת קְטַנָּה?
phrases.english: And why was one large and one small?
So that the craftsmen would take by the small one,
phrases.notes: The text is corrected from כשהיו to שהיו.

phrases.english: and return by the large one,
so that they would not come to misuse consecrated property.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָמָה הָיוּ אַחַת גְּדוֹלָה וְאַחַת קְטַנָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason behind the measures described in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Artisans are paid by the smaller measure and give back work by the larger one, in order to avoid מעילה.

steps.title: Why were two large cubits needed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why there were two large cubits, when one larger measure would seem to be enough for the safety margin.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need two?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short clarifying question about the משנה, and it is setting up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Comparing משה's cubit against a single larger cubit would already prevent מעילה. So the גמרא wants to know why a second large cubit, with a different size, was necessary.
steps.confusionAlert: The 'two' here means the two large cubits in שושן הבירה, the ½-אצבע one and the 1-אצבע one. It does not mean the large cubit and the small one.

phrases.english: Why do I need two?

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּרְתֵּי לְמָה לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the need for both large measures described in steps 1 and 2.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The separate purpose of each of the two enlarged cubits.

steps.title: One for gold and silver, one for building
steps.stepSummary: The smaller enlarged cubit was used for gold and silver work. The larger one was used for construction.
steps.simpleTranslation: One was for silver and gold, and one was for building.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that each large cubit had its own job.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Gold and silver are expensive, so even a small margin costs the craftsman a lot of money. For that work, the margin was kept to only half an אצבע. For cheaper building materials like wood and stone, a full אצבע margin was used.
steps.whatToRemember: There were three cubits: משה's standard cubit, a +½ אצבע cubit for precious metals, and a +1 אצבע cubit for construction.

phrases.english: One is for silver and gold,
and one is for building.

steps.triggerLanguage: חֲדָא דְּכַסְפָּא וְזַהֲבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ½-אצבע cubit was for precious metals, to limit the artisans' loss, and the 1-אצבע cubit was for construction.

steps.title: A different answer: the fingerbreadth of flesh between tail joints
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק (or רב הונא בר נתן) says the ברייתא's אצבע refers to our own משנה about blemishes: a full אצבע of flesh between joints.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק, and some say רב הונא בר נתן, said: it refers to what we learned in the משנה, where there is a full fingerbreadth of flesh between one joint and the next.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא gives a second answer to the earlier question of which law the ברייתא about an אצבע was meant for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of the Temple measuring cubits, he links the ברייתא to the blemish laws of a בכור in our משנה. There, a tail with a full אצבע of flesh between its joints counts as a מום. According to him, that אצבע is the one measured as a quarter of an average טפח.

keyTerms.meaning: And some say (introduces an alternate attribution)
It refers to that which we learned
A joint or vertebra (here, of the tail)

steps.whyThisMatters: It ties the general measurement rule directly to a practical blemish (מום) that can permit slaughtering a בכור.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי תֵּימָא רַב הוּנָא בַּר נָתָן,
phrases.english: and some say Rav Huna bar Natan, said:
it refers to that which we learned:
where there is flesh between one joint and the next
a full fingerbreadth.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק וְאִי תֵּימָא רַב הוּנָא בַּר נָתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different identification of the ברייתא's אצבע, as an alternative to the שושן הבירה source in steps 1–4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ברייתא's quarter-טפח אצבע applies to the blemish of a full אצבע of flesh between tail joints.

steps.title: The משנה: no testicles or only one testicle
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה lists two more blemishes for a בכור: having no testicles at all, or having only one testicle.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If it has no testicles, or if it has only one testicle, it counts as a blemish.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts. It adds two more blemishes that allow a בכור to be slaughtered: no testicles, or only one testicle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בכור may only be slaughtered outside the מקדש if it has a real מום. This משנה adds a problem with the testicles to the list. The גמרא will soon ask why both cases are needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה (the base text being studied)
A physical blemish that lets a בכור be slaughtered and eaten

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
It has no testicles,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ אֵין לוֹ אֶלָּא בֵּיצָה אַחַת.
phrases.english: or it has only one testicle.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ אֵין לוֹ בֵּיצִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה after the discussion of measurements and the אצבע.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בכור with no testicles, or with only one testicle, has a מום.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל: judge by the number of sacs
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל says that two sacs mean two testicles, and one sac means only one testicle.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל says: If it has two sacs, it has two testicles. If it does not have two sacs, it has only one testicle.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ישמעאל gives a simple way to decide: count the sacs on the outside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We often cannot see inside the animal, so רבי ישמעאל uses the outside as the sign. Two sacs mean the animal is complete, so it has no מום. One sac means it is treated as having one testicle, so it does have a מום.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who judges by what can be seen from outside

phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael says:
If it has two sacs,
it has two testicles;
if it does not have two sacs,
it has only one testicle.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a way to decide when the animal counts as having one testicle.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The number of sacs tells us the number of testicles.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: check by pressing the sac
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא says to sit the animal on its rump and press the sac. If a testicle is there, it will come out.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: You seat it on its rump and press the sac. If there is a testicle there, it will eventually come out.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא disagrees with counting sacs. He says to do a physical test instead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא wants real checking, not a guess from outside signs. If pressing brings the testicle down, the animal is complete. If nothing comes out, we decide it has only one.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says:
One seats it on its rump and presses;
if there is a testicle,
it will eventually come out.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר מוֹשִׁיבוֹ עַל עַכּוּזוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי ישמעאל's sign and offers a physical test instead.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: We check by pressing the sac, not by counting sacs.

steps.title: The story of the hidden testicle
steps.stepSummary: The test was done and nothing came out. After slaughter, the testicle was found stuck to the loins. רבי עקיבא permitted the meat; רבי יוחנן בן נורי forbade it.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a case where someone pressed and nothing came out. The animal was slaughtered, and the testicle was found stuck to the loins. רבי עקיבא permitted it, and רבי יוחנן בן נורי forbade it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה tells a real story that tested רבי עקיבא's method. They argued about whether the meat could be eaten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The test showed a מום, so the animal was slaughtered. Later a second testicle was found, stuck to the loins. רבי עקיבא permits the meat, since a testicle that did not come down to its place counts as missing, so this is a real מום. רבי יוחנן בן נורי forbids it, since the animal really had both testicles and so had no מום.

keyTerms.meaning: A story / real case that happened
A תנא who argues with רבי עקיבא here

steps.confusionAlert: רבי עקיבא is not saying the test excuses an error. He holds that a testicle stuck in the loins, which never came out, really is a מום. That is why the ברייתא later has him accuse רבי יוחנן בן נורי of wasting money on animals that may be eaten.

phrases.english: There was a case where one pressed and it did not come out;
it was slaughtered, and it was found stuck to the loins;
and Rabbi Akiva permitted
and Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri prohibited.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַעֲשֶׂה שֶׁמִּיעֵךְ וְלֹא יָצָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows a case where רבי עקיבא's test gave the wrong result.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the test failed and the testicle was found later, רבי עקיבא permits and רבי יוחנן בן נורי forbids.

steps.title: Why mention no testicles at all
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if one testicle is already a מום, it is obvious that having none is a מום.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Now that you said having only one testicle is a blemish, do we even need to say that having none at all is a blemish?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the order of the משנה. The first case seems unnecessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If missing one testicle is a מום, then missing both is clearly a מום too. So listing 'no testicles' adds nothing. The question is phrased like a question, but it really attacks the wording of the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה
Now that (opens a 'this is even more obvious' argument)

phrases.english: GEMARA:

phrases.aramaic: הַשְׁתָּא אֵין לוֹ אֶלָּא בֵּיצָה אַחַת
phrases.english: Now, if it has only one testicle
you said it is a blemish,
if it has none at all, is it necessary to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשְׁתָּא אֵין לוֹ אֶלָּא בֵּיצָה אַחַת אָמְרַתְּ הָוֵי מוּמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the opening line of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The line 'אין לו ביצים' in the משנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the smaller lack (one testicle) is a מום, the bigger lack (none) is obviously a מום, so listing it is unnecessary.

steps.title: The משנה is missing words
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה is missing text. It really means: two testicles in one sac, or two sacs with one testicle, is a מום.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה is missing words, and this is what it is teaching: If it does not have two testicles in two sacs, but in one sac, or if it has two sacs with one testicle, this is a blemish.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the problem by saying the משנה is missing some words. Now the משנה describes two new cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'No testicles' really means 'not two testicles in two sacs,' because both are in one sac. 'Only one testicle' means two sacs but only one testicle inside. These are not obvious, so the extra line is no longer a problem.

keyTerms.meaning: Words are missing from the text
And this is what it teaches

steps.confusionAlert: After this fix, 'אין לו ביצים' no longer means the animal has zero testicles. It means the two testicles are not each in their own sac.

phrases.english: It is missing words,
and this is what it teaches:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לוֹ שְׁתֵּי בֵּיצִים בִּשְׁתֵּי כִּיסִין
phrases.english: It does not have two testicles in two sacs,
but in one sac,

phrases.aramaic: אִי נָמֵי שְׁתֵּי כִּיסִין וּבֵיצָה אַחַת —
phrases.english: or alternatively, two sacs and one testicle;
this is a blemish.

steps.triggerLanguage: חַסּוֹרֵי מִיחַסְּרָא וְהָכִי קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא by rereading the משנה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה lists zero testicles and one testicle, which repeats itself.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה lists two different cases: two testicles in one sac, and two sacs with one testicle.
steps.whyThisMatters: This new reading changes how we understand the argument between רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא in the next steps.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל in the fuller version
steps.stepSummary: In the fixed reading, רבי ישמעאל says two sacs mean we know there are two testicles, and one sac is treated like only one testicle.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל says: If it has two sacs, we know it has two testicles. If it has only one sac, it is treated like an animal that has only one testicle.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps reading the fixed משנה. It explains רבי ישמעאל's view according to the new cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With two sacs, רבי ישמעאל assumes two testicles, so the case of 'two sacs, one testicle' never becomes a מום for him. With one sac, it is a מום even if both testicles are there. The sac is what decides for him.

keyTerms.meaning: Like one that does not have

phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael says:
If it has two sacs,
it is known that it has two testicles;
if it has only one sac,

phrases.aramaic: כְּמִי שֶׁאֵין לוֹ אֶלָּא בֵּיצָה אַחַת דָּמֵי,
phrases.english: it is considered like one that has only one testicle.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אוֹמֵר יֵשׁ לוֹ שְׁתֵּי כִּיסִים בְּיָדוּעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the fixed version of the משנה, now for רבי ישמעאל.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי ישמעאל was only talking about a missing testicle.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי ישמעאל, the number of sacs decides everything: two sacs means no מום, one sac means a מום.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא rejects 'it is known'
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא says we do not assume two testicles just because there are two sacs. Instead, we press the sac to check.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי עקיבא comes to say: We do not say 'it is known.' Rather, one seats it on its rump and presses. If there is a testicle, it will eventually come out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what רבי עקיבא is arguing against in the fixed version. He rejects רבי ישמעאל's assumption.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל trusts two sacs as proof of two testicles. רבי עקיבא says this is not proof. We must press and see, and if nothing comes out, it has only one testicle and has a מום.

keyTerms.meaning: And he comes (to add or argue)

steps.whatToRemember: In the fixed reading, the argument is about two sacs. רבי ישמעאל assumes two testicles are inside, while רבי עקיבא says to check by pressing.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Akiva comes to say:
We do not say 'it is known';
rather, one seats it on its rump and presses;
if there is a testicle, it will eventually come out.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲתָא רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא לְמֵימַר בְּיָדוּעַ לָא אָמְרִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows רבי עקיבא's disagreement with רבי ישמעאל in the fixed version.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two sacs do not prove two testicles; we press the sac to check.

steps.title: Quoting the story from the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the story line from the משנה to set up a ברייתא about it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: And there was a case where one pressed and it did not come out, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה. It is setting up the next step, where a ברייתא gives more details.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is only a heading that points back to the story in step 9. It adds nothing new by itself. It tells us the next source explains this story.

phrases.english: And there was a case where one pressed and it did not come out, etc.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַעֲשֶׂה שֶׁמִּיעֵךְ וְלֹא יָצָא וְכוּ׳
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the argument to the story at the end of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Introduces the story from the משנה for more explanation.

steps.title: רבי יוסי names where the story happened
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא from רבי יוסי says the story happened in פירן of בית מנחם. It repeats that רבי עקיבא permitted and רבי יוחנן בן נורי forbade.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: רבי יוסי said: There was a case in פירן of בית מנחם where someone pressed and it did not come out. The animal was slaughtered, and the testicle was found stuck to the loins. רבי עקיבא permitted it, and רבי יוחנן בן נורי forbade it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that adds the place where the story happened. The ruling is the same as in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new detail is the place: פירן of בית מנחם. This shows the story really happened. The argument between רבי עקיבא and רבי יוחנן בן נורי stays exactly the same.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא
The תנא who tells the story
A place name where the story happened

steps.whatToRemember: The hidden-testicle story was a real case in פירן of בית מנחם. רבי עקיבא permits the meat because a testicle that did not come out counts as a מום. רבי יוחנן בן נורי forbids it because the animal really had both testicles, so it had no מום.

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Yosei said:
There was a case in Piran of Beit Menaḥem
where one pressed and it did not come out,
and it was slaughtered, and it was found stuck to the loins,
and Rabbi Akiva permitted,
and Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri prohibited.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי מַעֲשֶׂה בְּפָירָן שֶׁל בֵּית מְנַחֵם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds details to the story quoted in step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The story happened in פירן of בית מנחם; רבי עקיבא permitted and רבי יוחנן בן נורי forbade.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא says רבי יוחנן בן נורי is wasting people's money
steps.stepSummary: In the ברייתא, רבי עקיבא criticizes רבי יוחנן בן נורי for forbidding the animal, because this makes the owners lose money.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא said to רבי יוחנן בן נורי: How long will you keep wasting the money of ישראל?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues the story from Step 15. רבי עקיבא, who permitted the animal, sharply criticizes רבי יוחנן בן נורי, who forbade it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא holds that the animal has a מום, so the owner may slaughter and eat it. If you say it has no מום, the owner cannot eat it and loses its value. So in רבי עקיבא's eyes, forbidding it wastes Jewish money for no reason.

keyTerms.meaning: Until when? How long? (an expression of sharp criticism)
The money or property of the Jewish people

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva said to Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri:
Until when will you waste
the money of the Jewish people!
phrases.notes: By forbidding animals that really have a blemish.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא quoted in Step 15 with the words the two תנאים exchanged.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי עקיבא holds that forbidding this animal causes a needless loss of money.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן בן נורי answers that רבי עקיבא is feeding people forbidden meat
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן בן נורי answers back that רבי עקיבא is causing ישראל to eat נבילות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן בן נורי said to רבי עקיבא: How long will you keep feeding ישראל נבילות?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן בן נורי answers רבי עקיבא's criticism with a criticism of his own. He says that permitting the animal makes people eat forbidden meat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי יוחנן בן נורי's view, permitting the animal is not just a money question. It causes a real איסור. As the ברייתא is quoted here, he calls that איסור 'נבילות', and the גמרא will now question that word.

keyTerms.meaning: Animals that died without proper שחיטה

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי לְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri said to Rabbi Akiva:
Until when will you feed
the Jewish people unslaughtered carcasses!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי לְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reply to רבי עקיבא's criticism in Step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן בן נורי holds that permitting the animal leads to eating forbidden meat.

steps.title: The animal was properly slaughtered, so how can it be called נבילה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the animal was properly slaughtered, so the word נבילות does not fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: But wasn't it properly slaughtered?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the word רבי יוחנן בן נורי used. A נבילה is an animal that was not slaughtered properly, but this animal was slaughtered correctly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two תנאים argued about whether this animal has a מום. They did not argue about its שחיטה. So the word 'נבילות' cannot describe the problem.

phrases.english: Wasn't it properly slaughtered?

steps.triggerLanguage: לָאו מִישְׁחָט שַׁחְטֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the exact word used in Step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The word 'נבילות' in רבי יוחנן בן נורי's reply
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: נבילה means an animal without valid שחיטה. This animal had valid שחיטה, so the term is wrong.

steps.title: Suggestion: he meant טריפות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that he really said 'טריפות', not 'נבילות'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he said: טריפות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to fix the wording. Maybe רבי יוחנן בן נורי said that רבי עקיבא was feeding people טריפות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A טרפה is forbidden even after a perfect שחיטה. So this word would avoid the problem from Step 18.

keyTerms.meaning: Animals with a fatal defect, forbidden even after proper שחיטה

phrases.english: Rather, he said: tereifot.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: טְרֵיפוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 18 by changing the word.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The reply says נבילות, which does not fit a slaughtered animal.
steps.terutzMaskana: Read it as טריפות, which can apply to a slaughtered animal.

steps.title: But this case has nothing to do with טרפה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion, because the argument has nothing to do with טריפות.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is not a question of the איסור of טריפות!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the fix from Step 19. Nobody claims this animal has a deadly defect, so 'טריפות' does not fit either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Having one sac or one testicle is about a מום on a בכור. It is not about whether the animal will die. So both suggested words, נבילות and טריפות, describe the wrong איסור.

keyTerms.meaning: The prohibition of eating a טרפה

phrases.english: But it is not a prohibition of tereifot!

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא אִיסּוּר טְרֵיפוֹת הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer of Step 19.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The argument is about whether this is a מום. It is not about a fatal defect, so טרפה is not the issue.

steps.title: Final reading: eating קדשים outside the Temple
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that he said 'You are feeding ישראל קדשים בחוץ'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he said: How long will you keep feeding ישראל holy animals outside the Temple?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the correct version of רבי יוחנן בן נורי's words. His complaint was that the animal is still holy, and it is being eaten outside the Temple.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן בן נורי holds that this is not a מום, so the בכור keeps its full holiness. Eating it outside the עזרה is the איסור of קדשים בחוץ. This fits the real argument, which is whether a מום exists.

keyTerms.meaning: Holy animals designated for the Temple

steps.whatToRemember: The real argument is about the מום. For רבי עקיבא, there is a blemish, so the owner may eat the animal, and forbidding it wastes money. For רבי יוחנן בן נורי, there is no blemish, so eating it is eating קדשים בחוץ.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוחנן בן נורי's complaint is not about a bad שחיטה or a sick animal. The words נבילות and טריפות were both rejected. His point is that the animal is still holy.

phrases.english: Rather, he said: Until when will you feed
the Jewish people sacrificial animals outside the Temple!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: עַד מָתַי אַתָּה מַאֲכִיל יִשְׂרָאֵל קָדָשִׁים בַּחוּץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected reading of Step 19 with a version that fits.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The complaint was about נבילות or טריפות.
steps.terutzMaskana: The complaint was about eating a still-holy בכור outside the Temple.

steps.title: New משנה: blemishes of the legs
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists more blemishes: five legs, three legs, closed hooves like a donkey's, שחול, and כסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: An animal with five legs, or one with only three, or one whose legs are closed like a donkey's, or the שחול or the כסול, has a מום.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins and lists blemishes connected to the legs. Any of these counts as a מום, so a בכור with it may be slaughtered and eaten outside the Temple.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list moves to the legs. Too many legs, too few legs, and hooves that are not split all count as blemishes. The משנה also names two terms, שחול and כסול, which it will define next.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
An animal with five legs,
or one that has only three,
or one whose legs are closed like those of a donkey,
phrases.notes: The hooves are solid, not split.

phrases.english: or the shachul, or the kasul.

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּעַל חָמֵשׁ רַגְלַיִם, אוֹ שֶׁאֵין לוֹ אֶלָּא שָׁלֹשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the ברייתא discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Five legs, three legs, closed hooves, שחול, and כסול are all blemishes.

steps.title: The משנה defines שחול and כסול
steps.stepSummary: The משנה explains the two terms. A שחול has a dislocated thigh. A כסול has one thigh higher than the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is a שחול? One whose thigh became dislocated. And a כסול? One whose thighs are uneven, with one higher than the other.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה asks and answers its own question to explain the two unusual words it just used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both are problems with the hip or thigh. A שחול has a thigh bone that slipped out of place. A כסול was built uneven, so one hip sits higher than the other.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal whose thigh is dislocated
An animal with one thigh higher than the other
Its thigh slipped out of its socket

phrases.english: What is a shachul?
One whose thighbone was dislocated.
And a kasul?
One with one of its thighs higher than the other.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיזֶהוּ שָׁחוּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the two terms listed at the end of Step 22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שחול means a dislocated thigh. כסול means uneven thighs.

steps.title: רב הונא: an extra or missing back leg also makes it a טרפה
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא limits the משנה to the front legs. An extra or missing back leg makes the animal a טרפה too, since an extra limb counts like a missing one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: The משנה only taught this about an extra or missing front leg. But for a back leg, the animal is also a טרפה, because anything extra is treated as if it were removed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with רב הונא explaining the משנה's case of five or three legs. He says the משנה only means a front leg.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a front leg, the animal just has a מום and may be eaten once slaughtered. With a back leg, it is also a טרפה, so it cannot be eaten at all. The reason is the rule that an extra limb counts like a missing limb, and a missing back leg makes an animal a טרפה.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who limits the משנה here
They only taught this in the case of
Anything extra counts as if it were removed

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a practical limit. Not every extra or missing leg is just a blemish. With a back leg, the animal becomes a טרפה and is completely forbidden to eat.
steps.confusionAlert: The rule 'extra counts like missing' can seem backwards. The idea is that an extra limb is treated as a defect, just like a missing one, so an extra back leg is judged like a missing back leg.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Rav Huna says:
They taught this only
where it was missing or had an extra front leg,
but with a hind leg, it is also a tereifa,
because any extra limb is like a removed one.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁחָסֵר וְיָתֵר בַּיָּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the משנה's case of five or three legs (Step 22) to the front legs.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An extra or missing front leg is only a מום. An extra or missing back leg also makes the animal a טרפה, because an extra limb counts as a removed one.

steps.title: Round hooves count even if split
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא rules that hooves rounded like a donkey's are a מום even if they are still split.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Do not think this is a מום only when the hooves are round and not split at all. Once they are round, it is a מום even if they are split.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא explains the משנה's case of hooves that are 'closed like a donkey's'. He tells us how wide this מום really is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We might have thought the animal needs a fully solid hoof, exactly like a donkey. רב פפא says the round shape alone is enough to make it a מום. A split down the middle does not save the animal.

keyTerms.meaning: do not say / do not think

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read רב פפא as requiring both round AND unsplit. He is saying the opposite: being round is enough, even if the hoof is split.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa says:
Do not say [only] where they are round and not split,
rather, once they are round,
even though they are split [it is a blemish].

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: לָא תֵּימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the closed-hooves case from the משנה in step 22 and defines its scope.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Round, donkey-like hooves are a מום even if they are split.

steps.title: ברייתא defines שחול and כסול
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא defines שחול as a dislocated thigh, and כסול as one leg in its socket and one leg above it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said 'the שחול and the כסול'. The רבנן taught: What is a כסול and what is a שחול? A שחול is an animal whose thigh slipped out of place. A כסול is an animal with one leg inside the hip socket and one leg above the hip socket.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words and brings a ברייתא that defines these two leg blemishes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שחול has a thigh fully out of its joint. A כסול is uneven: one leg sits properly and the other sits too high. This makes the animal's two sides unequal.

keyTerms.meaning: animal with one leg higher than the other

phrases.english: [The mishna said:] 'Or the shachul, or the kasul,' etc.
The Sages taught:
Which is a kasul and which is a shachul?
A shachul is one whose thigh was dislocated;
a kasul is one with one leg inside the hip socket
and one leg above the hip socket.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַשָּׁחוּל וְהַכָּסוּל וְכוּ׳. תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֵיזֶהוּ כָּסוּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the ברייתא's source and fuller wording for the definitions summarized in step 23.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שחול means a dislocated thigh. כסול means one leg sits in the socket and the other sits above it.

steps.title: ברייתא defines שרוע and קלוט
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא defines the Torah's שרוע as an animal with one stretched-out thigh, and קלוט as an animal with closed hooves like a donkey or horse.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: What are the שרוע and the קלוט? A שרוע is an animal whose thigh is stretched out longer. A קלוט is an animal whose hooves are closed like a donkey's or a horse's.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ברייתא. It defines two Torah words for blemished animals that are similar to the leg blemishes just discussed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These are the Torah's own terms for disqualified animals (ויקרא כב:כג). קלוט is the same closed-hoof case that רב פפא just explained in step 25. So this ברייתא gives that case a Torah source.

keyTerms.meaning: animal with one limb stretched longer

steps.whyThisMatters: It links the משנה's closed-hoof blemish to the Torah's word קלוט.

phrases.english: It was taught: The sarua and the kalut —
a sarua is one whose thigh became stretched out;
a kalut is one whose legs [hooves] are closed
like those of a donkey and like those of a horse.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא: הַשָּׂרוּעַ וְהַקָּלוּט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds related Torah-term definitions after the ברייתא on שחול and כסול.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שרוע means one thigh is stretched out. קלוט means hooves closed like a donkey's or a horse's.

steps.title: משנה: a broken leg bone is a blemish
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה rules that a broken foreleg or hind-leg bone is a מום even if it cannot be seen.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If the bone of its front leg or the bone of its back leg broke, it is a מום, even though the break is not visible.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins and adds another blemish to the list: a broken leg bone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Most מומין are things you can see. Here, a hidden break still counts as a מום. What makes it a מום is the broken bone itself, not how the leg looks.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
If the bone of its foreleg or the bone of its hind leg was broken,
even though it is not noticeable [it is a blemish].

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ נִשְׁבַּר עֶצֶם יָדוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the גמרא's discussion of leg blemishes.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A broken leg bone is a מום even when the break is not visible.

steps.title: אילא listed these blemishes in יבנה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה reports that אילא listed these מומין in יבנה, and the חכמים agreed with him.
steps.simpleTranslation: אילא listed these מומין in יבנה, and the חכמים agreed with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה tells us where this list of מומין came from. It also tells us that the חכמים accepted it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אילא was an expert on the מומין of a בכור. Because the חכמים agreed with him, his whole list became accepted halacha. This line also sets up the next step, where he adds more מומין.

keyTerms.meaning: a Sage who was an expert on blemishes
Yavne, the seat of the Sages after the Churban

phrases.english: These blemishes Ila enumerated in Yavne,
and the Sages agreed with him.

steps.triggerLanguage: מוּמִין אֵלּוּ מָנָה אִילָא בְּיַבְנֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the list of מומין by naming its source and its acceptance.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The list of מומין comes from אילא, and the חכמים accepted it.

steps.title: אילא adds three blemishes the חכמים had not heard
steps.stepSummary: אילא adds three more מומין: a round human-like eye, a pig-like mouth, and most of the speaking part of the tongue removed. The חכמים say they had not heard of these.
steps.simpleTranslation: אילא added three more. They said to him: We have not heard of these. They are: an eyeball that is round like a person's, a mouth that looks like a pig's, and an animal that lost most of the part of the tongue used for speaking.
steps.whatsHappening: אילא offers three more מומין. The חכמים do not accept them right away, because they have no tradition about them. This sets up the ruling in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים do not say the three are wrong. They only say they have no tradition about them, and the next step tells how a later בית דין settled the question. Each of the three is an unusual shape or a missing part.
steps.confusionAlert: 'We have not heard of these' does not mean the חכמים rejected אילא. It means they had no tradition, so they held back from ruling.

phrases.english: And he added three more;

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: לֹא שָׁמַעְנוּ אֶת אֵלּוּ.
phrases.english: they said to him: We have not heard of these.
[An animal] whose eyeball is round like a person's,
or whose mouth resembles a pig's,
or that lost most of the speaking part of its tongue.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעוֹד שְׁלֹשָׁה הוֹסִיף, אָמְרוּ לוֹ: לֹא שָׁמַעְנוּ אֶת אֵלּוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 29: after his accepted list, אילא proposes three more מומין.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אילא proposes three more מומין, and the חכמים of his time hold back because they have no tradition about them.

steps.title: Later court accepts the three blemishes
steps.stepSummary: The בית דין of the next generation rules that each of אילא's three additions is a מום.
steps.simpleTranslation: The בית דין that came after them said: This is a מום.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends by settling the question from the last step. A later בית דין accepts all three of אילא's added מומין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the חכמים held back because they had no tradition. The next generation's בית דין ruled that each one is a real מום. So all three now allow a בכור to be slaughtered.

keyTerms.meaning: the court of the following generation

steps.whatToRemember: All the מומין in this chapter come from אילא's list in יבנה. His three extra ones (round eye, pig-like mouth, most of the speaking part of the tongue removed) were later accepted as מומין too.

phrases.english: The court after them said:
This is a blemish.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּית דִּין שֶׁל אַחֲרֵיהֶן אָמְרוּ: הֲרֵי זֶה מוּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the open question about אילא's three additions from step 30.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A later בית דין ruled that each of אילא's three added cases is a מום.

steps.title: How can a flaw nobody sees be a blemish?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה's ruling that a broken leg bone is a מום even when it is not visible.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: If it cannot be seen, is it really a מום?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by questioning the משנה. A מום normally has to be on a visible part of the body, so how can a hidden break count?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, on 37b, we learned that a מום must be in an exposed place. The משנה here calls an unseen broken bone a מום, and that seems to clash with the rule. The גמרא wants to know how both can be true.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה
It is not noticeable or visible
A blemish that disqualifies a בכור from the מזבח

phrases.english: Gemara:
phrases.notes: The start of the גמרא section on this משנה

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ נִיכָּר, מִי קָא הָוֵי מוּמָא?
phrases.english: It is not noticeable — is it a blemish?!
phrases.notes: A מום must be in a visible place

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵינוֹ נִיכָּר, מִי קָא הָוֵי מוּמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the משנה from Step 28
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that a broken leg bone is a מום even though it is not visible
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A מום must be visible (37b), so an invisible break should not count

steps.title: The break is seen in how the animal walks
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that the leg itself looks normal, but the break shows when the animal moves.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: It is not noticeable by itself, but it is noticeable through its work.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the challenge. "Not visible" only means the leg's shape looks normal. The break still shows in the animal's walk.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer narrows what the משנה meant by "not noticeable." The flaw cannot be seen by looking at the leg, but it is noticeable from how the animal functions. Because it can still be detected from the outside, it fits the rule that a מום must be visible.

keyTerms.meaning: On its own account, meaning by its own appearance
On account of its work, meaning through its walking or activity

steps.whatToRemember: A hidden broken bone counts as a מום because the limp makes it noticeable.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
It is not noticeable on its own account,
but it is noticeable on account of its work.
phrases.notes: You can see it in how the animal walks

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: אֵינוֹ נִיכָּר מֵחֲמַת עַצְמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 32
steps.terutzMaskana: It means only that the leg's appearance is normal; the break is detectable through the walk

steps.title: Does this mean animals don't normally have round eyes?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about אילא and infers that a human-like round eye must be unusual for animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: "These blemishes he listed," etc. Is this to say that this is not their normal way?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the line about אילא's list and draws an inference. If a round human-like eye is a מום, it must be abnormal for animals. This is a setup for the contradiction that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מום is by definition something unusual. Calling the round eye a מום implies that animals do not normally have it. The גמרא pins down this assumption so that it can test it against another source.

keyTerms.meaning: Is this to say? (introduces an inference)

phrases.english: "These blemishes he listed," etc.
Is this to say that this is not its normal way?
phrases.notes: A round eye must be abnormal for animals

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמֵימְרָא דְּלָאו הַיְינוּ אוֹרְחֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to אילא's additions and draws out their implication
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a round human-like eye is really abnormal for animals

steps.title: A miscarried animal-shaped fetus and רבי מאיר's ruling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא raises a contradiction from a משנה in נדה. There, רבי מאיר rules that a woman who miscarries an animal-shaped fetus has the status of one who gave birth.
steps.simpleTranslation: They contrasted it: A woman who miscarries something shaped like a domestic animal, wild animal or bird, whether non-kosher or kosher, sits the days of a male if it is male. If it is female, she sits the days of a female. If it is unknown, she sits for both male and female. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה from מסכת נדה to set up the contradiction. Here it only quotes the ruling; the reason behind it comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר treats an animal-shaped miscarriage like a human birth for טומאת יולדת. That suggests these animals share some human feature. The next step names that feature, and that is where the clash with אילא will show.

keyTerms.meaning: And they contrasted it, meaning a contradiction is raised from another source
She sits, meaning she keeps the days of impurity and purity

steps.confusionAlert: This משנה is not about בכורות at all. It is brought only because of the reason behind it, which is about how an animal's eye looks.

phrases.english: And they contrasted it:
A woman who miscarries a type of domestic animal, wild animal, or bird,
whether non-kosher or kosher,
if it is male, she sits the days for a male.
If it is female, she sits the days for a female,
if it is unknown, she sits for a male and for a female,
phrases.notes: She follows the stricter side of each

phrases.english: these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּרְמִינְהוּ: הַמַּפֶּלֶת מִין בְּהֵמָה וְחַיָּה וָעוֹף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the opposing source that will challenge the inference of Step 34
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference that a round human-like eye is abnormal for animals
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי מאיר treats animal-shaped fetuses like humans, which suggests that animals share a human feature

steps.title: רבי מאיר's reason: animals have round eyes like people
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains that רבי מאיר's reason is that these animals' eyes are round like a person's. This contradicts אילא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: What is רבי מאיר's reason? Since its eyeball is round like a person's!
steps.whatsHappening: This step completes the contradiction. According to רבי יוחנן, all animals have round eyes like people, so how can אילא call a round eye a מום?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר's whole reason rests on animals naturally having human-like round eyes. If that is their normal nature, a round eye should not count as a מום. The source used for this challenge is רבי יוחנן's explanation, not the ruling itself.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: And Rabba bar bar Ḥana said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
What is the reason of Rabbi Meir?

phrases.aramaic: הוֹאִיל וְגַלְגַּל עֵינוֹ עָגוֹל כְּשֶׁל אָדָם!
phrases.english: Since its eyeball is round like that of a person!
phrases.notes: So round eyes are normal for animals, which contradicts אילא

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר? הוֹאִיל וְגַלְגַּל עֵינוֹ עָגוֹל כְּשֶׁל אָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the reason that turns the משנה in נדה into a contradiction
steps.kashyaTarget: אילא's ruling that a round human-like eye is a מום
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If all animals naturally have round eyes like people, a round eye cannot be an abnormal flaw

steps.title: Black part of the eye versus white part
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף resolves the contradiction: one source speaks about the black part of the eye, the other about the white part.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: It is not difficult. This one is about the black part, and that one is about the white part.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף resolves the contradiction by saying the two sources describe different parts of the eye.
steps.deeperAnalysis: As commonly explained, the white part of the eye is round in both animals and people, and that is what רבי מאיר relies on. אילא's מום refers to the black part being round like a human's, which is not normal for animals. So both sources stand.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; there is no contradiction
The black part of the eye
The white part of the eye

steps.whatToRemember: A round human-like eye is a מום when the black part is round. רבי מאיר's comparison to humans is based on the white part, which is naturally round in animals.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: It is not difficult,
this one is about the black part, that one is about the white part.
phrases.notes: Each source refers to a different part of the eye

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: לָא קַשְׁיָא, הָא בְּאוּכָּמָא, הָא בְּחִיוָּורָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in Steps 35-36
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (two different parts of the eye)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both sources speak about the same feature, the roundness of the eye
steps.terutzMaskana: אילא's מום concerns the black part; רבי מאיר's reason concerns the white part, which is naturally round

steps.title: רב פפא defines a pig-like mouth
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case of a mouth like a pig's. רב פפא rules that the upper lip only needs to overlap the lower lip. The mouth does not also need to be pointed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'Or its mouth is similar to a pig's.' רב פפא said: Do not say this means only a mouth that is both pointed and overlapping. Rather, once the upper lip overlaps, it is a blemish, even if the mouth is not pointed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new line from the משנה about a pig-like mouth, and רב פפא explains exactly what it means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A pig's snout is both pointed and has an upper lip hanging over the lower one. We might have thought the animal must look like a pig in both ways to count as blemished. רב פפא says the overlap alone is enough. The pointed shape is not required.

keyTerms.meaning: Pointed or narrowed, like a pig's snout
Overlapping. The upper lip hangs over the lower lip
'Do not say.' This introduces a reading that is being rejected

phrases.english: Or its mouth is similar to that of a pig.
phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה's list of blemishes.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
Do not say it means only where it is pointed and overlapping,
rather, once it overlaps,
even though it is not pointed, it is a blemish.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא תֵּימָא דִּשְׁפִיד וּפְרִוס, אֶלָּא כֵּיוָן דִּפְרִוס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next blemish in the משנה, after finishing the discussion of the eye.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An overlapping upper lip alone is the 'pig-like mouth' blemish, even if the mouth is not pointed.

steps.title: Whose view is the tongue rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case of an animal whose tongue was mostly cut off at the 'speaking' part. It asks which תנא holds this view.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'Or most of the speaking part of its tongue was removed.' Whose opinion is this משנה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next blemish and asks which Sage the משנה follows. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה does not just say 'most of the tongue.' It says 'most of the speaking part of the tongue.' That specific wording suggests the משנה follows one particular opinion, so the גמרא wants to know whose.

keyTerms.meaning: The 'speaking' part of the tongue. This is the part that matches the part a person uses to speak
'Whose view is our משנה?' A standard question asking which תנא the משנה follows

phrases.english: Or that most of the speaking part of its tongue was removed.
Whose opinion is our משנה?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִיתִין מַנִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next blemish in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that the blemish depends on the 'speaking' part of the tongue.

steps.title: It is רבי יהודה, from a ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה follows רבי יהודה. It quotes a ברייתא in which רבי יהודה says the blemish requires most of the speaking part of the tongue to be removed.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is the view of רבי יהודה. A ברייתא teaches: 'Or most of the tongue was removed.' רבי יהודה says: most of the speaking part of its tongue.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by showing a ברייתא where רבי יהודה uses the same wording as our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion in the ברייתא says 'most of the tongue.' רבי יהודה narrows it to 'most of the speaking part.' Our משנה uses רבי יהודה's wording, so the משנה follows him.

keyTerms.meaning: 'As it was taught.' This introduces a ברייתא
A תנא whose view our משנה follows here

steps.whatToRemember: The tongue blemish in our משנה follows רבי יהודה. What matters is most of the 'speaking' part of the tongue, not simply most of the tongue.

phrases.english: It is the view of Rabbi Yehuda,
as it was taught in a baraita: Or that most of the tongue was removed;
Rabbi Yehuda says:
most of the speaking part of its tongue.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הִיא, דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 39.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה follows רבי יהודה, as shown by his matching wording in the ברייתא.

steps.title: New משנה: the protruding lower jaw
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה tells of an incident in which a בכור's lower jaw stuck out past its upper jaw. רבן גמליאל asked the חכמים, and they ruled it a מום.
steps.simpleTranslation: And there was an incident where the lower jaw stuck out past the upper jaw. רבן גמליאל asked the חכמים, and they said: this is a blemish.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a real-life case about a jaw. The חכמים ruled that a lower jaw sticking out past the upper jaw is a blemish.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because this is a מום, the בכור may be slaughtered. Notice the משנה opens with 'and,' as if it continues an earlier rule. The גמרא will ask about this next.

keyTerms.meaning: An incident, a real case that happened
The נשיא who brought the question to the חכמים
Blemish. It allows a בכור to be slaughtered

phrases.english: MISHNA:
And there was an incident where the lower jaw
protruded beyond the upper jaw,
and Rabban Gamliel asked the Sages,
and they said: That is a blemish.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַעֲשֶׂה שֶׁהַלְּחִי הַתַּחְתּוֹן עוֹדֵף עַל הָעֶלְיוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה begins.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A lower jaw that protrudes beyond the upper jaw is a מום.

steps.title: Why does the משנה say 'and an incident'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what earlier teaching the word 'and' connects to, since the משנה opens with 'and there was an incident.'
steps.simpleTranslation: What did the תנא teach earlier that he now continues by saying 'And there was an incident'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices that the משנה starts with 'and' and asks what earlier rule this story is attached to. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a story is told to support a rule that was just taught. The previous lines did not mention a jaw at all. So the גמרא asks which earlier rule this story is meant to illustrate.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What did he teach?' This asks what earlier teaching is being continued

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not 'why is this a blemish?' It is about the extra word 'and.' The גמרא wants to know which earlier rule this story connects to.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
What did the tanna teach earlier, that he now teaches: 'And there was an incident'?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי תַּנָּא דְּקָתָנֵי וּמַעֲשֶׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the opening word of the משנה in step 41.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which earlier rule the story of the protruding jaw is connected to.

steps.title: The story limits the pig-mouth dispute
steps.stepSummary: The story connects to the earlier 'pig-like mouth' case, where the רבנן disagreed with רבי. Their dispute is only about an upper lip that sticks out. When the lower jaw sticks out, everyone agrees it is a מום.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because we learned earlier: 'its mouth is similar to a pig's,' and the רבנן disagree with רבי. So we say: the רבנן disagree with רבי only when the upper lip sticks out past the lower one. But when the lower sticks out past the upper, everyone agrees it is a blemish.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the story links back to the pig-like mouth case. It shows where the רבנן and רבי disagree and where they agree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the earlier case, the רבנן argued with רבי (the Sefaria translation identifies him as רבי אילא) about whether a pig-like mouth is a blemish. The story teaches that this argument covers only an upper lip that overlaps. A protruding lower jaw is a blemish according to everyone, as the חכמים told רבן גמליאל.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And we say.' This introduces the point the story is teaching

steps.whatToRemember: The 'pig-mouth' dispute is only about an overlapping upper lip. A protruding lower jaw is a מום according to everyone. That is why the משנה tells the story of רבן גמליאל with the word 'and.'
steps.whyThisMatters: The story narrows the earlier dispute to one specific case. It also makes the protruding lower jaw a blemish that everyone agrees on.

phrases.english: Because we learned: 'Its mouth is similar to a pig's,'
and the Rabbis disagree with Rabbi,
phrases.notes: The Sefaria translation identifies this as רבי אילא.

phrases.english: and so we say:
when the Rabbis disagree with Rabbi,
it is where its upper lip overlaps the lower one,
but where the lower protrudes beyond the upper,
everyone agrees it is a blemish.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם דִּתְנַן פִּיו דּוֹמֶה לַחֲזִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 42 by linking the story to the pig-mouth case discussed in step 38.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The story continues the pig-mouth rule. It shows that the dispute covers only an overlapping upper lip, while a protruding lower jaw is a blemish according to everyone.
